sections.subtitle: Formation with -mente
sections.content:
📋 Creating Adverbs from Adjectives

✅ Rule: Add -mente to feminine singular form

💡 Adjectives Ending in -O:
1️⃣ Change to -a
2️⃣ Add -mente

→ rápido → rápida → rápidamente (quickly)
→ lento → lenta → lentamente (slowly)

💡 Adjectives Ending in -E or Consonant:
• Add -mente directly

→ triste → tristemente (sadly)
→ feliz → felizmente (happily)
→ fácil → fácilmente (easily)

⚠️ Accent Preservation:
If adjective has accent, keep it!
→ rápido → rápidamente
→ difícil → difícilmente

🎯 Multiple Adverbs:
Only last one gets -mente
→ Habla clara y lentamente
  (clearly and slowly)

First stays as feminine adjective (clara), only last gets -mente (lentamente)

sections.subtitle: Adverbs of Time
sections.content:
📋 Time Adverbs

⏰ PRESENT/NOW:
• ahora (now)
• ya (already/now)
• todavía/aún (still)
• hoy (today)

⏩ FUTURE:
• luego (later/then)
• después (afterwards/later)
• mañana (tomorrow)
• pronto (soon)

⏪ PAST:
• ayer (yesterday)
• antes (before)
• anteayer (day before yesterday)
• recientemente (recently)

🔄 FREQUENCY:
• siempre (always)
• nunca/jamás (never)
• a veces (sometimes)
• muchas veces (often)
• casi nunca (hardly ever)
• todos los días (every day)

📍 SEQUENCE:
• primero (first)
• entonces (then)
• luego (then)
• finalmente (finally)

💡 Examples:
→ Ahora estoy ocupado (I'm busy now)
→ Siempre llego tarde (I always arrive late)
→ ¿Ya terminaste? (Did you finish already?)

sections.subtitle: Adverbs of Place
sections.content:
📋 Place Adverbs

📍 PROXIMITY:
• aquí/acá (here)
• ahí (there - near you)
• allí/allá (there - far)
• cerca (near/close)
• lejos (far)

➡️ DIRECTION:
• arriba (up/above)
• abajo (down/below)
• delante (in front)
• detrás (behind)
• dentro (inside)
• fuera (outside)

🌐 GENERIC:
• donde (where)
• adonde (to where)
• en todas partes (everywhere)
• en ningún sitio (nowhere)

💡 Examples:
→ Ven aquí (Come here)
→ El libro está ahí (The book is there)
→ Vivo cerca (I live nearby)
→ Vamos arriba (Let's go upstairs)

📍 Regional Note:
• aquí/allí more common in Spain
• acá/allá more common in Latin America
(Somewhat interchangeable)

sections.subtitle: Adverbs of Manner & Quantity
sections.content:
📋 Manner & Quantity Adverbs

✅ MANNER (how):
• bien (well)
• mal (badly)
• despacio (slowly)
• deprisa (quickly)
• así (like this/so)
• mejor (better)
• peor (worse)

💡 Examples:
→ Habla bien español (He speaks Spanish well)
→ Lo hice así (I did it like this)

⚠️ QUANTITY (how much):
• muy (very - with adjectives/adverbs)
• mucho (a lot - with verbs)
• poco (little)
• bastante (quite/enough)
• demasiado (too much)
• más (more)
• menos (less)

⚡ KEY DISTINCTION - MUY vs MUCHO:

✅ MUY (with adjectives/adverbs):
→ Es muy grande (It's very big)
→ Habla muy rápido (speaks very fast)

✅ MUCHO (with verbs):
→ Como mucho (I eat a lot)
→ Trabaja mucho (works a lot)

❌ Never: 'muy mucho'!

💡 More Examples:
→ Es muy inteligente (very intelligent)
→ Estudia bastante (studies quite a bit)

sections.subtitle: Comparative & Superlative Adverbs
sections.content:
📋 Comparing with Adverbs

✅ COMPARATIVE Forms:

• más + adverb + que (more...than)
→ Corro más rápido que tú
  (I run faster than you)

• menos + adverb + que (less...than)
→ Habla menos claramente que él
  (speaks less clearly than him)

• tan + adverb + como (as...as)
→ Trabajo tan duro como tú
  (I work as hard as you)

⚠️ IRREGULAR Comparatives:
• bien → mejor (better)
• mal → peor (worse)
• mucho → más (more)
• poco → menos (less)

💡 Examples:
→ Lo hago mejor que antes
  (I do it better than before)
→ Canta peor que yo
  (sings worse than me)

🎯 SUPERLATIVE:
Use 'lo' + más/menos + adverb (+ possible)

→ Lo más rápidamente posible
  (as quickly as possible)
→ Llegué lo más tarde que pude
  (I arrived as late as I could)

sections.subtitle: Position of Adverbs
sections.content:
📋 Where to Place Adverbs

✅ GENERAL RULE:
Adverbs usually follow the verb
→ Habla lentamente (speaks slowly)
→ Corro mucho (I run a lot)

💡 WITH COMPOUND TENSES:
Between auxiliary and participle OR after participle
→ He trabajado mucho ✅ (common)
→ He mucho trabajado (less common)

⚠️ WITH OBJECT:
After object
→ Leo libros frecuentemente ✅
→ Leo frecuentemente libros ❌

🔄 TIME/FREQUENCY ADVERBS:
More flexible - can start sentence
→ Siempre llego tarde ✅
→ Llego siempre tarde ✅
(Both OK)

⚡ NUNCA/JAMÁS:
Go before verb (no double negative needed)
→ Nunca como carne (I never eat meat)

🎯 FOR EMPHASIS:
Place at beginning
→ Rápidamente, corrí a casa
  (Quickly, I ran home)

📍 Key: Flexible placement, but follow verb is most common

questions.question: How do you form adverbs from adjectives ending in -o?
questions.hint: Rápido → rápida → rápidamente. Use feminine form first.

questions.question: What is the adverb form of 'rápido' (fast)?
questions.hint: Rápido → rápida (feminine) → rápidamente. Keep the accent!

questions.question: How do you form adverbs from adjectives ending in -e or consonants?
questions.hint: Triste → tristemente, fácil → fácilmente. Just add -mente.

questions.question: What is the adverb form of 'feliz' (happy)?
questions.hint: Ends in consonant, so add -mente directly: felizmente.

questions.question: 'Habla clara y lentamente' - Why not 'claramente y lentamente'?

answers.text: With multiple adverbs, only last one gets -mente

questions.hint: Efficiency rule: first adverb(s) stay as feminine adjective, only last gets -mente.

questions.question: What does 'ahora' mean?
questions.hint: Present time adverb: Ahora estoy ocupado (I'm busy now).

questions.question: What does 'luego' mean?
questions.hint: Future time adverb: Luego voy al cine (I'll go to the movies later).

questions.question: What does 'siempre' mean?
questions.hint: Frequency adverb: Siempre llego tarde (I always arrive late).

questions.question: What does 'nunca' or 'jamás' mean?
questions.hint: Negative frequency: Nunca como carne (I never eat meat).

questions.question: '¿Ya terminaste?' means...
questions.hint: Ya = already/now. Often used in questions about completion.

questions.question: What does 'aquí' mean?
questions.hint: Place adverb: Ven aquí (Come here).

questions.question: 'Allí' vs 'ahí' - What's the difference?

answers.text: Allí is formal, ahí is informal

questions.hint: Ahí is closer (there near you), allí is farther away (over there).

questions.question: What does 'arriba' mean?
questions.hint: Direction: Vamos arriba (Let's go upstairs).

questions.question: 'Habla bien español' - What does 'bien' modify?
questions.hint: Bien = well (adverb of manner). Modifies how he speaks.

questions.question: 'Es muy grande' vs 'Como mucho' - Why muy vs mucho?

answers.text: Muy modifies adjectives/adverbs; mucho modifies verbs
Muy is formal, mucho is informal

questions.hint: MUY + adjective/adverb (very big). MUCHO + verb (eat a lot).

questions.question: Is 'muy mucho' correct?

answers.text: No, never use muy and mucho together

questions.hint: NEVER combine muy and mucho. Use one or the other based on what you're modifying.

questions.question: 'Trabaja mucho' means...
questions.hint: Mucho modifies verb: trabajar mucho = to work a lot.

questions.question: 'Corro más rápido que tú' means...

answers.text: I run as fast as you

questions.hint: Más + adverb + que = more...than (comparative).

questions.question: What is the irregular comparative of 'bien' (well)?
questions.hint: Bien has irregular comparative: mejor (not 'más bien'). Lo hago mejor (I do it better).

questions.question: What is the irregular comparative of 'mal' (badly)?
questions.hint: Mal has irregular comparative: peor (not 'más mal'). Canta peor (sings worse).

questions.question: 'Trabajo tan duro como tú' means...

answers.text: I work as hard as you
I work less hard than you

questions.hint: Tan + adverb + como = as...as (equality comparison).

questions.question: Where do adverbs usually go in Spanish sentences?

answers.text: At the end of sentence always

questions.hint: General rule: verb + adverb. Habla lentamente (speaks slowly).

questions.question: 'Nunca como carne' - Why is there no 'no' before the verb?

answers.text: Nunca before verb doesn't need 'no' (no double negative)
It's an error, should be 'no nunca'

questions.hint: When nunca/jamás goes BEFORE verb, no 'no' needed. After verb needs 'no': No como nunca.

questions.question: 'He trabajado mucho' vs 'He mucho trabajado' - which is more common?

answers.text: He trabajado mucho (after participle is more common)
He mucho trabajado (between is more common)

questions.hint: With compound tenses, adverb typically goes after participle, though between is possible.
